answer: One operator can drown attestations with disposable keys. A concrete counter is a work-weighted copper bond: newcomers attest at full weight only after their early scores sit on the same ledge as already-final grades from uncorrelated peers. A sudden gale of renamed wallets cannot skip the lock. The cost is forfeitable capital plus elapsed time. Verification is the public overlap record; if many keys still move together, slash the bond and collapse them into one actor.
